data.context_sentence: My boss wants the report on his desk by noon.
data.context_translation: הבוס שלי רוצה הדוח על השולחן שלו עד הצהריים.
data.correct_answer: My boss wants the report on his desk by noon.
data.common_mistake: "By noon" = before twelve o'clock. "On his desk" = physical location.

data.context_sentence: Please restart your computer after you install the update.
data.context_translation: אנא הפעל מחדש המחשב אחרי שאתה מתקין העדכון.
data.correct_answer: Please restart your computer after you install the update.
data.common_mistake: "Restart" = turn off and on again. "Reboot" is similar.

data.context_sentence: The rain stopped and the sun came out again.
data.context_translation: הגשם הפסיק והשמש יצאה שוב.
data.correct_answer: The rain stopped and the sun came out again.
data.common_mistake: "The sun came out" = clouds cleared and sun appeared.

data.context_sentence: The teacher gave us homework for the weekend.
data.context_translation: המורה נתן לנו שיעורי בית לסוף השבוע.
data.correct_answer: The teacher gave us homework for the weekend.
data.common_mistake: "Homework" is uncountable — no "homeworks".

data.context_sentence: Our flight was delayed because of bad weather.
data.context_translation: הטיסה שלנו עוכבה בגלל מזג אוויר גרוע.
data.correct_answer: Our flight was delayed because of bad weather.
data.common_mistake: "Delayed" = late. "Cancelled" = did not happen at all.

data.context_sentence: By the way, did you remember to call your mother?
data.context_translation: אגב, זכרת להתקשר לאמא שלך?
data.correct_answer: By the way, did you remember to call your mother?
data.common_mistake: "By the way" introduces extra information — often at the start or end of a sentence.

data.context_sentence: Yesterday, she ___ to the market.
data.context_translation: אתמול, היא ___ לשוק.
data.common_mistake: "Go" is irregular. Past Simple: go → went. Never "goed."

data.context_sentence: They ___ a new car last month.
data.context_translation: הם ___ מכונית חדשה בחודש שעבר.
data.common_mistake: "Buy" is irregular. Past Simple: buy → bought. Rhymes with "thought" and "caught."

data.context_sentence: I ___ a letter to my friend.
data.context_translation: כתבתי מכתב לחברי.
data.common_mistake: "Write" is irregular: write → wrote → written. Past Simple is "wrote" (no "d" or "ed").

data.context_sentence: We ___ the train to the city centre.
data.context_translation: לקחנו את הרכבת למרכז העיר.
data.common_mistake: "Take" is irregular: take → took → taken. Past Simple is "took."

data.context_sentence: He ___ to the manager about the problem.
data.context_translation: הוא ___ עם המנהל על הבעיה.
data.common_mistake: "Speak" is irregular: speak → spoke → spoken. Do not say "speaked."

data.context_sentence: I ___ that film three times already.
data.context_translation: כבר ___ את הסרט הזה שלוש פעמים.
data.common_mistake: "See" irregular past participle: see → saw → seen. Present Perfect: have/has + seen.

data.context_sentence: She ___ sushi many times — she loves Japanese food.
data.context_translation: היא ___ סושי הרבה פעמים — היא אוהבת אוכל יפני.
data.common_mistake: "Eat" irregular: eat → ate → eaten. With "she/he/it" use "has eaten", not "have eaten."

data.context_sentence: They ___ the record for the fastest marathon time.
data.context_translation: הם ___ את השיא לזמן המרתון המהיר ביותר.
data.common_mistake: "Break" irregular: break → broke → broken. Present Perfect uses "broken" (past participle), not "broke."

data.context_sentence: She ___ English every evening.
data.context_translation: היא ___ אנגלית כל ערב.
data.common_mistake: Verbs ending in consonant + y: change "y" to "i" and add "-es". study → studies, carry → carries.

data.context_sentence: He ___ the news every morning before breakfast.
data.context_translation: הוא ___ חדשות כל בוקר לפני ארוחת הבוקר.
data.common_mistake: Verbs ending in -ch, -sh, -x, -ss, -o add "-es": watch → watches, finish → finishes.

data.context_sentence: The results ___ announced at the end of the week.
data.context_translation: התוצאות ___ יוכרזו בסוף השבוע.
data.common_mistake: This is passive future: "will be + past participle (announced)." Just conjugate "be" with "will" here.

data.context_sentence: We ___ to Argentina next spring.
data.context_translation: אנחנו ___ לארגנטינה באביב הבא.
data.common_mistake: "Going to" + base verb. With "we": "we are going to travel." Indicates a planned decision.

data.context_sentence: She ___ on the presentation when the power cut off.
data.context_translation: היא ___ על המצגת כשהחשמל נכבה.
data.common_mistake: Past Continuous: was/were + verb-ing. Describes an ongoing past action interrupted by another event.

data.context_sentence: They ___ to music when I arrived.
data.context_translation: הם ___ למוזיקה כשהגעתי.
data.common_mistake: With "they/we/you", use "were + -ing". With "I/she/he/it", use "was + -ing."

data.context_sentence: Look! He ___ towards the finish line.
data.context_translation: תסתכל! הוא ___ לקראת קו הסיום.
data.common_mistake: Double the final consonant before adding -ing for short vowel + consonant verbs: run → running, sit → sitting.

data.context_sentence: I ___ a student.
data.context_translation: אני ___ תלמיד.
data.common_mistake: Use "am" with "I", "is" with he/she/it, "are" with you/we/they.

data.context_sentence: She ___ chocolate.
data.context_translation: היא ___ שוקולד.
data.common_mistake: Add -s for he/she/it in Present Simple: "She likes" not "She like".

data.context_sentence: They ___ to the park on Sundays.
data.context_translation: הם ___ לפארק בימי ראשון.
data.common_mistake: With they/we/you/I, use the base verb: "They go" — no -s.

data.context_sentence: They ___ the project before the deadline was moved forward.
data.context_translation: הם ___ את הפרויקט לפני שהדדליין הוקדם.
data.common_mistake: Past Perfect: had + past participle. Use when one past action happened before another.

data.context_sentence: It ___ that the policy will be revised next quarter.
data.context_translation: ___ שהמדיניות תתוקן ברבעון הבא.
data.common_mistake: Passive reporting structure: "It is considered that…" = people consider that…

data.context_sentence: She ___ at home yesterday evening.
data.context_translation: היא ___ בבית אתמול בערב.
data.common_mistake: Past Simple of "be": I/he/she/it → was. We/you/they → were.

data.context_sentence: They ___ very happy at the party last night.
data.context_translation: הם ___ מאוד שמחים במסיבה אתמול בלילה.
data.common_mistake: With they/we/you use "were" in the past — never "was".

data.context_sentence: She ___ two brothers and one sister.
data.context_translation: יש ___ שני אחים ואחות אחת.
data.common_mistake: "Have" for possession: I/you/we/they → have. She/he/it → has.

data.context_sentence: He ___ a headache yesterday, so he stayed home.
data.context_translation: היה ___ לו כאב ראש אתמול, אז הוא נשאר בבית.
data.common_mistake: Past of "have" (possession or experience) = "had" for all persons.

data.context_sentence: I ___ cooking dinner when the doorbell rang.
data.context_translation: ___ מבשל ארוחת ערב כשצלצל פעמון הדלת.
data.common_mistake: Past Continuous: was/were + verb-ing. With "I" use "was" — then add the main verb (-ing form follows "was").
